Yes. There was once a popular web forum that was officially for a shock/everything-nothing website in the 1990s and 2000s, but came to be its own thing. On the site, you could give someone positive or negative "reputation". This affected a colored reputation meter underneath that poster's portrait. When leaving reputation, you had the option of adding a brief comment. Leaving reputation was anonymous, but some people found it customary to "sign" it using the comment space. To avoid abuse, you couldn't leave reputation for one specific user more than one until you left reputation for a variety of others, probably like 10-15 people, and you could only leave reputation a few times per 24 hours. Get someone's reputation low enough, and they can't raise/reduce your reputation any more, but can still leave a comment.

So I would have a rotation of people I disliked there, who received negative reputation on a regular, repeating basis, as a means of refreshing my arsenal for leaving positive reputation for others.

The negative reputation annoyed people to no end. They would badger mods to find out who did it, and such and then they would start hitting you back with negatives, maybe even get their friends to gang up on you.

It was a fun diversion.
